title: 2002 AMC 10B Problem 25
statement: When \(15\) is appended to a list of integers, the mean is increased by \(2.\) When \(1\) is appended to the enlarged list, the mean of the enlarged list is decreased by \(1.\) How many integers were in the original list?

solutions.text:
Let the original list have \(n\) integers with mean \(m,\) so its sum is \(mn.\) Appending \(15\) gives \[ \begin{aligned} &(m + 2)(n + 1) \\ &= mn + 15 \\ &\implies m + 2n = 13. \end{aligned} \]

Appending \(1\) to that enlarged list gives \[ \begin{aligned} &(m + 1)(n + 2) \\ &= mn + 16 \\ &\implies 2m + n = 14. \end{aligned} \]

Solving \(m + 2n = 13\) and \(2m + n = 14\) yields \(m = 5\) and \(n = 4.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
